record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: Fix an even degree j > 2. Let F be a general degree-j form in n variables and Γ = Spec(S/Ann(F)) ⊆ A^n. For most pairs (j, n), does [Γ] lie on a unique elementary component that is everywhere nonreduced? If that is too strong, can one at least exhibit one pair (j, n) for which this happens?

evidence.quote: Problem XIX (Odd behaviour of even degrees). Fix an even j > 2. Let F be a general form of degree j in n variables. Let Γ = Spec(S/ Ann(F)) ⊆ A^n. Is it true that then [Γ] ∈ Hilbd(A^n) lies on a unique elementary component which is everywhere nonreduced for “most” pairs (j, n)? Can one at least find one such pair?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $S = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables, and let $T = k[y_1,\dots,y_n]$ act on $S$ by contraction (partial differentiation). For a form $F \in S$ of degree $j$, define the apolar (annihilator) ideal $\mathrm{Ann}(F) = \{\partial \in T : \partial \circ F = 0\} \subseteq T$, and consider the zero-dimensional Gorenstein subscheme $\Gamma = \mathrm{Spec}(T/\mathrm{Ann}(F)) \subseteq \mathbb{A}^n$ of some length $d$. The Hilbert scheme of points $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ then has a point $[\Gamma]$. An irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ is called elementary if its general point parameterizes a scheme supported at a single point.

Fix an even integer $j > 2$. For a general form $F$ of degree $j$ in $n$ variables, determine for which pairs $(j,n)$ the point $[\Gamma]$ lies on a unique elementary irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ which is moreover everywhere nonreduced. As a weaker version: exhibit at least one pair $(j,n)$ with even $j > 2$ for which this conclusion holds.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem on deformations of Artinian algebras and Hilbert schemes. Related work has constructed new elementary components of the Gorenstein locus and shown the Gorenstein locus is non-reduced for n > 9, but no published result confirms the specific "unique everywhere nonreduced elementary component" claim for general even-degree apolar Gorenstein points in the stated generality. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: New elementary components of the Gorenstein locus of the Hilbert scheme of points
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs new elementary components of the Gorenstein locus, including nonreduced ones, via apolar algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions exhibit elementary components in the Gorenstein locus but do not settle the even-degree question in general.

status_evidence.title: Elementary components of Hilbert schemes of points (Jelisiejew)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies elementary components arising from apolar/compressed algebras and identifies cases of nonreduced behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Provides framework but does not resolve the posed conjecture for all even j>2 and most n.
